**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Handle non-fast-forward before pushing sync commit**

The final `git push` assumes `main` has not advanced since checkout, so concurrent merges can cause a non-fast-forward rejection (`fetch first`) and fail this job. In that case the canonical change is merged but the duplicated `SKILL.md` files and `caveman.skill` are not updated, and they can stay stale until another canonical edit retriggers this workflow. Add a pull/rebase-and-retry (or equivalent) step before pushing the bot commit.

If `CAVEMAN_DEFAULT_MODE=off` (or config default is `off`), prompts like "talk like caveman" create `~/.claude/.caveman-active` containing `off`, which makes statusline/reporting inconsistent with the intended "off means no active flag" behavior. **<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Avoid full-mode reinforcement for commit/review modes**

This reminder text is emitted for every active mode, including `commit`, `review`, and `compress`, but the injected guidance is the base caveman rule set (`Drop articles...` and `Code/commits/security: write normal.`). After users switch to `/caveman-commit` or `/caveman-review`, each turn now gets instructions that conflict with those specialized modes, so outputs can regress to normal prose instead of the expected commit/review behavior. Restrict this reinforcement to base intensity modes (`full/lite/ultra/wenyan*`) or emit mode-specific context for independent modes.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Nest SessionStart command under a hooks matcher group**

This `hooks.json` entry is not in Codex’s expected three-level hook shape (`event -> matcher group -> hooks[]`): the `SessionStart` item has `type`/`command` at the matcher-group level instead of inside a `hooks` array. Codex deserializes `SessionStart` as matcher groups, so this object yields an empty group and no handler executes, meaning plugin installs will not auto-activate Caveman as documented. Wrap the command inside `{"hooks": [{"type": "command", ...}]}` (and optional `matcher`) so SessionStart actually runs.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Scope negation check to activation intent**

The negation guard in `process.stdin.on('end')` rejects activation whenever `don't` or `do not` appears anywhere in the prompt, so valid inputs like `activate caveman, don't use markdown` will no longer turn the mode on. Fresh evidence in this commit is that `no` was removed and tested, but `don't|do not` are still matched globally here, preserving the same false-negative class for common follow-up constraints. Limit this check to negating activation phrases (for example `don't activate` / `do not activate`) or to tokens before the activation trigger.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Narrow activation guard to caveman-adjacent negations**

The expanded negative guard now includes bare `end`, `cancel`, `off`, and `no` anywhere in the prompt, so activation is skipped even when the user explicitly asks to enable caveman mode (for example, prompts like “no kidding, go caveman” or “use caveman mode, no emojis”). This introduces silent activation failures and leaves mode tracking inconsistent with user intent; restrict these checks to explicit caveman-adjacent deactivation phrases (such as `no caveman`/`caveman off`) instead of global word matches.

Adding `end|cancel|exit` to the broad deactivation alternation causes unlinking whenever those common words appear in a prompt that also mentions `caveman`, even if the user is not trying to disable the mode (e.g., “go caveman and end with a summary”). Because the regex allows arbitrary text between tokens, ordinary instructions can now deactivate caveman unexpectedly; constrain these to explicit stop phrases like `end caveman`/`cancel caveman mode` instead of sentence-wide co-occurrence.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Handle UTF-8 BOM when parsing project frontmatter**

`readProjectDefaultMode()` requires the file to start with `---`, but many Windows editors save UTF-8 files with a BOM (`\uFEFF`) prefix, so `.claude/caveman.local.md` becomes valid-looking yet silently ignored and resolution falls through to global/default mode. This makes per-project defaults fail in a common setup; strip an initial BOM before matching or accept it in the frontmatter regex (for example `^\uFEFF?---`).

`createProxyAwareFetch` only re-resolves the proxy per hop while it stays inside its own manual redirect loop. If the very first hop is exempted by NO_PROXY, `proxy-fetch.ts:247` returns `baseFetch(input, init)` directly without ever entering that loop, so Node's native fetch follows every subsequent redirect on its own with `redirect: "follow"`. Any later hop that lands outside NO_PROXY and should go through HTTP_PROXY is fetched directly instead. The same thing happens mid-chain: the non-proxied branch at line 265 also calls `baseFetch` with `redirect: "follow"`, so once any hop in the chain is unproxied, every hop after it is too, silently.

This matters here because a redirect through a bypassed internal host back out to a proxy-only target is a normal pattern (e.g. an internal short-link or mirror before hitting the real CDN), and it is exactly the shape `caveman setup --install` needs to survive on a proxy-only egress host.

```
$ node --test tests/proxy-fetch-repro.runtime.mjs
not ok 1 - a request that starts at a bypassed host and redirects out to a proxied target reaches the real target directly, skipping the proxy
  error: the second hop should have gone through the proxy stub
  + actual - expected
  + []
  - [ '/final' ]
```

`proxy.seen` stays empty: the stub HTTP_PROXY is never contacted for the second hop, even though its target is not in NO_PROXY.

Fix direction: drop the early return at line 247 and always enter the loop, using `redirect: "manual"` (not `"follow"`) for the direct-fetch branch at line 265-270 too, so every hop's Location header goes through the same `resolveProxyUrl` call regardless of whether the previous hop was proxied.

The content class in the new pattern, `[^`]+`, still forbids any backtick inside a span, so a shorter complete backtick pair nested inside a longer delimiter's interior gets matched first and splits the outer span instead of becoming its literal content. ['([^']
